issues.body:
docs/branch-protection.md:13-14 (§Protected branch, unchanged by this diff) reads:

    - **`main`** — the only long-lived branch. All changes land via pull request; direct
      pushes are disallowed (including for administrators — see "Other settings").

The new §Other settings text (diff hunk 1, now lines 426-430) says the opposite: the live ruleset carries a repository-role bypass actor with `bypass_mode: always`, i.e. an administrator CAN push directly to `main`. The stale sentence does not merely coexist with the correction — it explicitly directs the reader to "Other settings" as its own supporting evidence, so the two statements are wired together and a reader following the pointer lands on the refutation.

This is the headline claim of the document (§Protected branch is the first substantive section), and this PR's entire purpose is to remove exactly this overclaim. Leaving it in the same file is an incomplete correction, and for a compliance doc-of-record an internally contradictory record is worse than a uniformly wrong one: neither statement can be relied on.
issues.fix_hint: Update docs/branch-protection.md:13-14 in this PR to match §Other settings, e.g.: "All changes land via pull request; direct pushes are disallowed for non-administrators. Repository administrators retain an always-on ruleset bypass (see §Other settings) — the automated landing flow does not use it." Then re-grep the file for any other unqualified enforcement-is-uniform wording before landing.
issues.title: Doc now contradicts itself: line 14 still claims direct pushes are disallowed "including for administrators", and points at the section this PR reversed

issues.body:
Three compliance artifacts name docs/branch-protection.md as their evidence source for precisely the claim this PR retracts:

- compliance/openssf/controls/openssf.md:26 — Branch-Protection control, evidence string ends "... block force-push/deletion, no bypass actors."
- compliance/slsa/controls.md:142 — SL-S-c, "`docs/branch-protection.md` (… block branch deletion, no admin bypass)".
- compliance/slsa/evidence.md:125 — Two-person review (AR), "`docs/branch-protection.md` (… no admin bypass)".

After this PR those three control claims are false, and they are false in the audit-facing direction (asserting a protection that is not enforced). They cannot be caught by re-reading the source doc either, because the source doc no longer says what they quote.

This is also a violation of the file's own rule at docs/branch-protection.md:576-578: "If a future check finds drift … update **this table and the matching section above in the same commit** so the doc-of-record never lags the live ruleset." The spirit of that rule — no lagging record of the ruleset — extends to the compliance docs that quote it, since they are the artifacts an auditor actually reads.

(Filed against docs/branch-protection.md because the verdict schema requires a path present in the diff; the edits belong in the three compliance files.)
issues.fix_hint: In this same PR, update the three evidence strings to match the corrected doc — drop "no bypass actors" / "no admin bypass" and replace with the honest form, e.g. "repository-administrator bypass present (bypass_mode: always); the automated landing path does not use it and remains constrained by merge-queue admission, squash-only, no force-push, no deletion". If either OpenSSF Branch-Protection or SLSA SL-S-c is thereby no longer fully satisfied, record it in compliance/openssf/gap-register.md rather than restating the weakened claim as met. Separately, compliance/slsa/evidence.md:125 still claims "≥1 approving review, require-code-owners, dismiss-stale", which docs/branch-protection.md:521 states are 0/false/false — pre-existing drift worth fixing while in that file.
issues.title: Downstream compliance evidence still cites this doc for "no bypass actors" / "no admin bypass" — not updated in the same commit as the doc's own drift rule requires

issues.body:
The new heading at docs/branch-protection.md:426 is "**Repository administrators have an emergency bypass.**", but the value recorded one line later is `bypass_mode: always`. GitHub's bypass modes are `always` and `pull_request` (request-based); there is no "emergency"/break-glass mode, and `always` encodes no situational limit whatsoever. The word "emergency" implies a control (invoked only under declared exception) that the configuration does not implement — exactly the kind of soft overclaim this PR is otherwise removing.

The body text immediately after is honest ("an explicit exception to uniform enforcement, not a compensating control"), so only the heading is out of step. Worth tightening because this file is cited as compliance evidence and headings are what get quoted.

Related, smaller: the prose infers "repository administrators" from `actor_id: 5` without recording the role name the API returns. Recording the resolved role alongside the id makes the next reconciliation check mechanical.
issues.fix_hint: Retitle to something the config supports, e.g. "**Repository administrators can always bypass the ruleset.**" — and, if the bypass is intended to be break-glass in practice, say so as a *policy* statement distinct from the enforced setting ("policy: used only for declared incidents; not enforced by the ruleset"). Optionally record the resolved role name from the `gh api …/rulesets/<id>` output next to `actor_id: 5`.
issues.title: "emergency bypass" overstates the constraint recorded: bypass_mode is `always`, not a break-glass mode

issues.body:
.github/workflows/bench.yml:378 ("the `main` ruleset (id 17688455: … EMPTY bypass list) rejects it with `GH013`") and .github/workflows/bead-autoclose.yml:36 ("ruleset GH013, empty bypass list — confirmed on the first real run") both assert the state this PR retracts.

The empirical conclusion in those comments is still correct — the default GITHUB_TOKEN / github-actions bot is not a repository administrator, so it is rejected whether or not an admin bypass actor exists — but the stated *reason* is now wrong, and bench.yml:394 goes on to propose "Option A — add the github-actions bot to the `main` ruleset bypass list" while describing that list as empty. A future reader reconciling the ruleset will hit the same contradiction.

Low severity: comments only, no behavioural effect, and both files are outside this diff.
issues.fix_hint: Amend both comments to say the bypass list contains only the repository-administrator role (no bot/app actors), so the GH013 rejection of GITHUB_TOKEN stands for the right reason. Can be folded into this PR or filed as a follow-up self-improvement issue.
issues.title: Two workflow comments still state the `main` ruleset has an EMPTY bypass list

verdict.summary:
Doc-only change that retracts a false claim ("empty bypass_actors / current_user_can_bypass: never") and records the real live state: a repository-role bypass actor (actor_id: 5, bypass_mode: always), plus a merge_queue row in the live-rules table. The direction is right and honesty-improving — it downgrades an overclaim in a compliance doc-of-record rather than strengthening one — and the merge_queue parameters (max_entries_to_merge: 8) are consistent with the pre-existing Omnibus-batching section (line 454). I could not independently verify the live ruleset: `gh` is not installed here, so the API values are taken at face value (the safe direction, since the claim is being weakened).

The correction is INCOMPLETE, which for a doc whose sole purpose is to be an accurate record is a correctness defect, not a nit:

1. The same file still asserts the retracted claim at line 14 — "direct pushes are disallowed (including for administrators — see 'Other settings')" — and that cross-reference points at the very section this PR rewrote to say the opposite. The doc-of-record now contradicts itself, self-referentially.

2. Three compliance documents still cite this doc for the retracted claim: compliance/openssf/controls/openssf.md:26 ("no bypass actors"), compliance/slsa/controls.md:142 and compliance/slsa/evidence.md:125 ("no admin bypass"). The file's own drift rule (lines 576-578) requires doc and dependents move together; leaving them stale means live compliance evidence asserts something this PR establishes as false.

Also minor: "emergency bypass" is not supported by the recorded bypass_mode: always (no break-glass constraint is encoded), and two workflow comments still state the bypass list is EMPTY.

No security or injection content in the diff; no code or tests affected.
